解析：return 限定票的用途，somewhere safe 是地点整体；不是要求立即返程。
下次：听到物品保管→记物品用途及保存状态→检查 return 修饰的对象。

S259.reference: Large bags go underneath, while smaller ones can stay with you.
S259.explanation:
读懂：大包放下面，小包可以随身带；ones 代指包。
解析：while 对照两类包的不同位置；smaller 与 Large 的对比方向不变。
下次：听到两类物品安排→分别配对大小与位置→核对替代词 ones。

S260.reference: We will wait here until everyone on the list has arrived.
S260.explanation:
读懂：名单上的人都到齐前，我们会在此等待。
解析：“名单上的所有人”作为范围；has arrived 对应 everyone，until 定等待终点。
下次：听到集合终点→记到齐的具体范围→检查 everyone 与完成状态。

S261.reference: If the first vehicle fills up, another one will leave ten minutes later.
S261.explanation:
读懂：第一辆坐满时，另一辆会晚十分钟出发。
解析：记“首车满／另车出发／晚十分钟”；one 代替 vehicle，later 是相对时间。
下次：听到备用安排→连接触发条件与替代选择→核对间隔而非钟点。

S262.reference: The driver will announce which entrance we should use when we reach the museum.
S262.explanation:
读懂：到博物馆时，司机会告知应从哪个入口进入。
解析：按“司机告知／用哪个入口／抵达时”记；which 从句内部用陈述语序。
下次：听到告知内容→先记谁通知，再记通知事项→核对入口与时间。

S263.reference: Please be back at this meeting point by four, even if you finish your visit earlier.
S263.explanation:
读懂：即使提前参观完，也请最迟四点回到这个集合点。
解析：by four 是最迟四点；even if 说明提前完成也适用这一安排，并非必须等到四点。
下次：听到 by 加钟点→记截止时间与地点→核对让步条件不改变最迟期限。

S264.explanation:
读懂：排练室里暖和；rehearsal 是“排练”。
解析：记“排练室／暖和”，warm 是状态而非正在变热的动作。
下次：听到房间描述→记地点与状态→检查连接动词。

S265.reference: Share a music folder with your neighbor.
S265.explanation:
读懂：和旁边的人合用一本乐谱夹；share 是“共用”。
解析：按“合用乐谱夹／与邻座”记，with 连接共用对象。
下次：听到 share→同时记共用物和同伴→核对 with。

S266.reference: Listen to the melody once before you try singing it.
S266.explanation:
读懂：先听一遍旋律，再尝试唱；melody 是“旋律”。
解析：once 限定听的次数，it 回指旋律；不要把次数移到唱的动作上。
下次：听到练习顺序→配对次数和动作→检查代词与先后。

S267.reference: Take a quiet breath wherever a small comma appears above the words.
S267.explanation:
读懂：歌词上方出现小逗号的地方，要轻轻换气。
解析：按“轻轻换气／出现逗号处／歌词上方”记；wherever 连接每个相应位置。
下次：听到标记对应动作→连记标记形状、位置和动作→核对轻重限定。

S268.reference: The lower voices enter two beats after the higher voices begin.
S268.explanation:
读懂：高声部开始两拍后，低声部进入；beats 指音乐的拍。
解析：记“低声部进入／晚两拍／相对高声部”；先后和间隔都重要。
下次：听到声部进入安排→先找参照事件→检查间隔与先后方向。

S269.reference: Do not speed up simply because the words become more familiar.
S269.explanation:
读懂：不要仅因歌词变熟悉就加速；speed up 是“加快”。
解析：主动作有否定；because 引出不应成为加速理由的情况。
下次：听到不要及原因→记被限制的动作→核对比较状态与因果范围。

S270.reference: Leave the chairs where they are when we finish.
S270.explanation:
读懂：结束后椅子保持原位；where they are 指现在的位置。
解析：分成“保留椅子／原处／结束时”；they 代指椅子。
下次：听到归位安排→辨别移动还是保留→核对地点从句与时间。

S271.explanation:
读懂：地图抽屉编有号码；numbered 表示“已编号”。
解析：记“地图抽屉／有编号”；are 对应复数 drawers。
下次：听到存储说明→记对象与识别方法→核对复数动词。

S272.reference: Use both hands to lift the sheet.
S272.explanation:
读懂：用双手拿起这张图；sheet 指一张纸。
解析：按“双手／拿起图纸”记；both 限定两只手都用。
下次：听到操作要求→连记动作与身体部位→核对 both。

S273.reference: These tables are wide enough to hold an unfolded map.
S273.explanation:
读懂：这些桌子够宽，能放下一张展开的地图。
解析：wide enough to 连起宽度和用途；unfolded 说明地图没有折起。
下次：听到 enough to→把尺寸与能做的事配对→检查否定前缀。

S274.reference: You may photograph the map as long as you turn off the flash.
S274.explanation:
读懂：关闭闪光灯的前提下，可以拍地图。
解析：许可与条件由 as long as 连接；turn off 是关掉，不能漏 off。
下次：听到有条件的许可→分别记允许行为和前提→检查动作方向。

S275.reference: Two maps with similar titles may show the same area in different years.
S275.explanation:
读懂：标题相似的两张地图可能表现同一地区的不同年份。
解析：分清“标题相似／地区相同／年份不同”；may 保留可能性。
下次：听到多项比较→逐项配对同与不同→核对可能性词。

S276.reference: Write down the reference number so another reader can locate the exact copy you used.
S276.explanation:
读懂：记下索引号，让其他读者能找到你用过的那份地图。
解析：三块是“记编号／帮助定位／同一份”；exact 限定精确到哪份。
下次：听到记录编号的目的→连接标识与定位对象→核对 exact 和 used。

S277.reference: Please ask us to put the maps away.
S277.explanation:
读懂：请让工作人员收好地图；put away 是“收起”。
解析：ask us to 表示请我们做；不能省 us 后变成自己收起的要求。
下次：听到请求协助→记实际执行者→核对 ask 后的人与动作。

S278.explanation:
读懂：地板现在已空出来；clear 指没有障碍物。
解析：按“地板／现在空着”记；clear 在此不是颜色浅。
下次：听到场地状态→联系场景理解形容词→检查时间词。

S279.reference: Stand with your feet slightly apart.
S279.explanation:
读懂：站立时双脚略微分开；slightly 是“稍微”。
解析：记站姿“脚稍分开”；apart 是分开状态，slightly 限制幅度。
下次：听到姿势要求→配对部位和状态→核对程度词。

S280.reference: Watch my feet first, and then try the steps yourself.
S280.explanation:
读懂：先看我的脚步，再自己尝试动作。
解析：first 与 then 给顺序；my 和 yourself 区分示范者与练习者。
下次：听到示范再练习→按人物和先后分块→核对两处人物指向。

S281.reference: The movement starts on your left, although I am facing the opposite direction.
S281.explanation:
读懂：on your left（在你的左侧）是动作起点；示范者朝向与你相反。
解析：主句以听者左侧为准；让步解释示范者朝向不同，不能直接照镜像换边。
下次：听到左右与朝向→先确定以谁为参照→核对对比连接词。

S282.reference: Change partners after each round so you can practice with different people.
S282.explanation:
读懂：每轮后换搭档，以便和不同的人练习。
解析：按“换搭档／每轮后／练习目的”记；each round 不能变成只换一次。
下次：听到循环安排→记周期与目的→检查 each 和 different。

S283.reference: If you lose the rhythm, listen for the beat before joining in again.
S283.explanation:
读懂：跟不上节奏时，先找拍子，再重新加入。
解析：三个块为“失去节奏／听拍子／再加入”；listen for 表示留意寻找声音。
下次：听到恢复步骤→按问题、线索、重启排序→核对 before 和 again。

S284.reference: Small, steady steps are better than large movements that you cannot control.
S284.explanation:
读懂：小而稳定的步伐，比无法控制的大动作更好。
解析：比较双方是小稳步与不可控大动作；cannot 限定后者。
下次：听到比较→保留双方特征→检查否定没有移到推荐做法上。

S285.explanation:
读懂：这个服务台处理失物；lost property 指遗失物品。
解析：记服务台及其职责；handles 是动词“处理”。
下次：听到机构职责→配对地点与业务→检查动词词尾。

S286.reference: Describe the item in your own words.
S286.explanation:
读懂：用自己的话描述物品。
解析：按“描述物品／用自己的话”记；own 强调由本人描述。
下次：听到描述要求→连记对象与表达方式→核对 in 和 own。

S287.reference: A color alone may not be enough to identify your bag.
S287.explanation:
读懂：仅凭颜色可能不足以确认你的包。
解析：alone 限制证据，may not be enough 保留可能不足而非完全没用。
下次：听到证据限制→保留程度和可能性→检查否定范围。

S288.reference: Tell us what was inside without looking at the contents first.
S288.explanation:
读懂：先别查看内容，告诉我们包里有什么。
解析：what was inside 是告知内容；without 后限制不能先看。
下次：听到身份核验→区分所需描述和禁用线索→核对 without。

S289.reference: Items found in classrooms are usually brought here at the end of the day.
S289.explanation:
读懂：教室里发现的物品，通常当天结束时送到这里。
解析：主语带“教室里发现”的限定；usually 说明通常安排，are brought 表示被送来。
下次：听到处理流程→记发现地点、频率和送达时点→核对被动。

S290.reference: If we receive something matching your description, we will contact you using the number on this form.
S290.explanation:
读懂：matching your description（与你描述相符的）限定收到的物品；之后用表上号码联系你。
解析：按“物品符合描述／联系你／用表上号码”记；条件与联系渠道均要保留。
下次：听到后续通知→连接触发条件、动作和渠道→核对物品限定。

S291.reference: Keep the reference slip until your item has been returned.
S291.explanation:
读懂：物品归还前，请保留查询凭条。
解析：until 给保留的终点，has been returned 表示物品已被归还。
下次：听到凭条用途→记保存期限→检查完成被动和物品归属。

S292.reference: Your projector is ready to collect.
S292.explanation:
读懂：投影仪可以领取了；projector 是“投影仪”。
解析：记“你的投影仪／准备可领”；ready to collect 是可领取状态。
下次：听到取用通知→配对设备与状态→检查 to collect。

S293.reference: The case contains two short cables.
S293.explanation:
读懂：盒里装有两根短线；contains 表示“内有”。
解析：数量 two 和长度 short 都修饰 cables；case 是容器。
下次：听到物品清单→配对数量、特征和物品→核对容器主体。

S294.reference: Test the connection with your own computer before leaving the desk.
S294.explanation:
读懂：离开服务台前，用自己的电脑测试连接。
解析：按“测试连接／用自己的电脑／离开前”分块；own 指本人的实际设备。
下次：听到预先检查→记测试对象和所用工具→检查 before。

S295.reference: If the picture is upside down, ask us to change the display setting.
S295.explanation:
读懂：画面倒置时，请工作人员调整显示设置。
解析：upside down 整块表示倒置；ask us to 说明由谁调整。
下次：听到设备问题→配对现象、处理者与动作→核对位置短语。

S296.reference: You can extend the loan unless another student has already reserved the equipment.
S296.explanation:
读懂：如果没有其他学生预订，可以延长借期；unless 表示“除非”。
解析：记允许延长与阻止延长的条件；has already reserved 指已有预约。
下次：听到 unless→找会取消许可的情况→核对 already 与完成结构。

S297.reference: Please return all the cables together.
S297.explanation:
读懂：请把所有连接线一起归还。
解析：all 限定全部，together 限定同时交回；短句也不能漏范围。
下次：听到归还要求→检查数量范围和交回方式→核对 all 与 together。

S298.reference: Equipment left outside the office after closing will not be checked in until the next morning.
S298.explanation:
读懂：关门后留在办公室外的设备，要到次日早上才办理归还登记。
解析：长主语是“关门后放门外的设备”；not…until 表示登记要等到次晨。
下次：听到长主语加 not until→先记适用设备→核对最早办理时点。

S299.reference: Your room is on the third floor.
S299.explanation:
读懂：房间在三楼；third 是序数“第三”。
解析：按“你的房间／三楼”记，on 连接楼层，third 不能当数量 three。
下次：听到楼层→记对象和序数→检查 on。

S300.reference: This key opens the courtyard gate.
S300.explanation:
读懂：这把钥匙可以打开院门；courtyard 是“院子”。
解析：主语是这把钥匙，对象是院门；opens 对应单数 key。
下次：听到钥匙用途→一一配对钥匙与门→核对单数动词。

S301.reference: Check the furniture list before you start unpacking your belongings.
S301.explanation:
读懂：打开行李整理物品前，先核对家具清单。
解析：先检查清单，后整理物品；belongings 是个人随身物品的集合。
下次：听到入住步骤→按先后分块→核对清单对象与 unpacking。

S302.reference: Any damage that you notice should be recorded on this form.
S302.explanation:
读懂：发现的任何损坏都应记在这张表上。
解析：“你发现的损坏”为主语块；should be recorded 保留应当被记录的要求。
下次：听到需记录的信息→圈定范围→核对被动与表格位置。

S303.reference: Your roommate has already arrived but will not be back until this evening.
S303.explanation:
读懂：舍友已到过这里，但今晚才回来。
解析：两个时间状态是“已经到达”与“今晚才返回”；not until 限定第二次回来。
下次：听到 already 与 not until→区分完成事件和待发生事件→核对时间归属。

S304.reference: You are welcome to rearrange the desks as long as both residents agree.
S304.explanation:
读懂：双方住户都同意时，可以重新摆放书桌。
解析：许可动作是调整桌位，as long as 引出条件；both 限定双方。
下次：听到许可→记动作与共同同意的前提→核对 both。

S305.reference: Please make sure the outer door closes behind you whenever you enter or leave.
S305.explanation:
读懂：每次进出时，请确认外门在身后关好。
解析：按“确认外门关闭／每次进出”记；whenever 覆盖两种动作，outer 限定外门。
下次：听到重复适用的要求→连记对象和触发动作→检查 or 与 whenever。

S306.reference: The fabric samples are over here.
S306.explanation:
读懂：布料样片在这边；fabric 是“布料”。
解析：记“布料样片／在这里”；samples 为复数，对应 are。
下次：听到材料位置→连记物品与方位→核对复数。

S307.reference: Choose two pieces of the same size.
S307.explanation:
读懂：选两片大小相同的布。
解析：数量 two 与 same size 配对；of 连接尺寸特征。
下次：听到选材要求→分别记数量和一致条件→核对 same。

S308.reference: I will show you how to thread the machine before you begin.
S308.explanation:
读懂：开始前，我会演示怎样给机器穿线；thread 是动词“穿线”。
解析：按“我演示／如何穿线／开始前”记；how to thread 为一个方法块。
下次：听到教学安排→连接示范者、方法和时点→核对 before。

S309.reference: Press the pedal gently until you become familiar with the speed.
S309.explanation:
读懂：熟悉速度前，轻轻踩踏板；pedal 是“踏板”。
解析：动作方式是 gently，until 给这一阶段的终点；familiar with 表示熟悉。
下次：听到练习调整→记方式与结束条件→核对 gently 和 with。

S310.reference: A straight line drawn on the cloth can help you guide the fabric.
S310.explanation:
读懂：画在布上的直线能帮你引导布料。
解析：“画在布上的直线”为主语块；can help 后接引导动作。
下次：听到辅助标记→连接标记位置与用途→核对 drawn 的修饰对象。

S311.reference: Stop and raise your hand if the thread becomes tangled.
S311.explanation:
读懂：线缠住时停下来并举手；tangled 是“缠结的”。
解析：条件触发两个动作“停／举手”；and 保留两项都需做。
下次：听到故障信号→连记条件与两个反应→检查并列动作完整。

S312.reference: Once the machine has stopped completely, we can examine why the stitches look uneven.
S312.explanation:
读懂：机器完全停下后，再检查针脚为何不均匀。
解析：按“完全停下／检查／针脚不匀原因”记；completely 与 uneven 都不能漏。
下次：听到检查前提→先记完成程度→核对 why 后的陈述语序。

S313.explanation:
读懂：你的展示位置准备好了。
解析：记“你的展位／已准备好”；ready 描述状态。
下次：听到准备通知→连记对象与状态→核对 your。

S314.reference: Put the title beneath your name.
S314.explanation:
读懂：把作品标题放在姓名下方；beneath 是“在下面”。
解析：两个文字要素以姓名为参照；标题在下，不能互换。
下次：听到排版位置→先找参照对象→检查上下关系。

S315.reference: The frames along this wall belong to students in the photography class.
S315.explanation:
读懂：这面墙边的画框属于摄影课的学生。
解析：按“墙边画框／属于／摄影课学生”分块；belong to 连起物品与所有者。
下次：听到归属→配对物品范围与人群→核对 to。

S316.reference: Measure the distance between the pictures before deciding where to place each label.
S316.explanation:
读懂：决定每个标签位置前，先量画作之间的距离。
解析：先量间距，后决定标签位置；between 的对象是图片，不是标签。
下次：听到布置顺序→分清测量物和放置物→核对 where to。

S317.reference: Leave enough room for visitors who want to step back and view the whole arrangement.
S317.explanation:
读懂：留出空间，让想后退观看整体布置的观众能站开。
解析：三块为“留空间／后退的观众／观看整体”；who 修饰 visitors，whole 限定全部布置。
下次：听到空间用途→连接人群、动作和观看范围→检查 whole。

S318.reference: Although the labels are small, they should still be easy to read from nearby.
S318.explanation:
读懂：标签虽小，仍应让近处的人容易看清。
解析：让步连接小尺寸与可读性；still 说明要求并未取消，nearby 限定距离。
下次：听到让步→分别记限制与仍需达到的效果→核对 still 和距离。

S319.reference: Keep the packaging until the exhibition closes.
S319.explanation:
读懂：展览结束前保留包装材料。
解析：按“保留包装／直到闭展”记；until 引出保存期限。
下次：听到材料保留要求→找结束事件→核对 until 与 closes。

S320.reference: We have your name badge here.
S320.explanation:
读懂：这里备有你的姓名牌。
解析：按“我们有／你的名牌／这里”记；your 与 here 都用于具体定位。
下次：听到报到通知→配对领取物与地点→核对所属词。

S321.reference: Coffee is available in the lobby.
S321.explanation:
读懂：大厅有咖啡供应；lobby 是“大厅”。
解析：记“咖啡供应／大厅里”；available 说明可以取用。
下次：听到服务地点→连记物品和位置→核对 in。

S322.reference: The printed program includes a map of all the meeting rooms.
S322.explanation:
读懂：纸质议程册中有所有会议室的地图。
解析：按“议程册／包括地图／所有会议室”记；all 限定覆盖范围。
下次：听到资料内容→配对载体与信息→核对 printed 和 all。

S323.reference: Sessions marked with a star have moved to the larger hall upstairs.
S323.explanation:
读懂：标有星号的场次已改到楼上更大的厅。
解析：主语由 marked with a star 限定；have moved 表明变更已发生。
下次：听到安排变更→先确定哪些场次→核对新地点及完成状态。

S324.reference: Please keep questions brief so the speakers have time to respond.
S324.explanation:
读懂：提问请简短，让发言者有时间回应。
解析：keep questions brief 是保持问题简短；so 引出目的，不能丢掉问答双方。
下次：听到发言要求→连记方式及目的→核对动作对象。

S325.reference: Anyone presenting a poster should be beside their display during the afternoon break.
S325.explanation:
读懂：展示海报的人应在下午休息时段守在展板旁。
解析：按“海报展示者／在展板旁／下午休息时”记；their 回指展示者。
下次：听到出席要求→配对人群、位置与时段→检查 should。

S326.reference: Because two workshops run at the same time, choose the one that best matches your interests.
S326.explanation:
读懂：两场工作坊同时举行，因此选最符合兴趣的一场。
解析：先记同时举行的原因，再记选择依据；the one 代替工作坊。
下次：听到冲突安排→连接限制与选择标准→核对替代词和比较程度。

S327.explanation:
读懂：我们两人一组玩；in pairs 指“成对”。
解析：记“我们玩／两人一组”；are playing 与分组方式一起保留。
下次：听到分组方式→记参与者和人数关系→核对 in pairs。

S328.reference: Each pair gets five blue counters.
S328.explanation:
读懂：每组得到五个蓝色筹码；counters 在此指游戏筹码。
解析：each pair 是每一组，five 与 blue 都限定筹码。
下次：听到分发规则→配对单位、数量和颜色→核对单数 gets。

S329.reference: Draw one card and read it aloud before moving your piece.
S329.explanation:
读懂：移动棋子前，抽一张卡并大声读出来。
解析：顺序是抽卡、读卡、移棋；it 指卡片，aloud 限定朗读方式。
下次：听到连续动作→按先后记物品→核对代词和方式词。

S330.reference: You may discuss the answer with your partner, but not with the other team.
S330.explanation:
读懂：可以与搭档讨论答案，但不能与另一队讨论。
解析：but not 对照两个讨论对象；may 表示允许，不是必须。
下次：听到许可及限制→分别记对象→核对否定所排除的人群。

S331.reference: If neither player knows the answer, put the card at the bottom of the pile.
S331.explanation:
读懂：两人都不知道答案时，把卡放回牌堆底部。
解析：neither 表示两者都不；动作终点为 bottom，不能变成顶部。
下次：听到 neither→保留双重人群范围→检查卡片归放位置。

S332.reference: The practice round does not count.
S332.explanation:
读懂：练习轮不计入正式结果。
解析：主语是练习轮，does not count 的否定决定规则。
下次：听到试用环节→核对是否计入→保留助动词和否定。

S333.reference: Once everyone understands the rules, we will reset the board and start a complete game.
S333.explanation:
读懂：所有人理解规则后，重置棋盘，再开始完整一局。
解析：按“大家理解／重置棋盘／正式开始”记；Once 指开始条件，complete 区别练习轮。
下次：听到正式开始安排→连接条件与两项动作→核对 complete。

S334.reference: Today's topic is on the board.
S334.explanation:
读懂：今天的辩题在板上。
解析：按“今天话题／板上”记；Today's 限定本次。
下次：听到话题位置→连记所属时间和位置→检查 on。

S335.reference: Choose a seat with your team.
S335.explanation:
读懂：和自己队伍坐在一起。
解析：动作是选座，with 说明与谁坐；your 指自己的队。
下次：听到入座要求→连接座位与同伴→核对 with。

S336.reference: Each speaker has two minutes to present an opening argument.
S336.explanation:
读懂：每位发言者有两分钟作开场论证。
解析：each speaker 对应 has；two minutes 是每人时限而非全队时限。
下次：听到发言时间→先找分配单位→核对数字和用途。

S337.reference: You may be asked to defend a position that you do not personally support.
S337.explanation:
读懂：do not personally support（本人不赞同）限定立场；仍可能被要求为它辩护。
解析：按“可能被要求／辩护立场／个人不赞同”记；后半否定修饰立场，不否定任务。
下次：听到分配立场→分清任务与个人意见→核对被动和否定范围。

S338.reference: Listen for the main claim rather than preparing your reply while someone else is speaking.
S338.explanation:
读懂：别人说话时，先听主要论点，而不是忙着准备回复。
解析：对比“听论点／准备回话”；while 给两项行为共同的时间背景。
下次：听到替代做法→记推荐与排除动作→核对时间范围。

S339.reference: A useful response explains why the evidence does or does not support the claim.
S339.explanation:
读懂：有效回应要解释证据为何支持或不支持论点。
解析：按“回应要解释／证据是否支持／论点”记；does or does not 保留两种可能。
下次：听到论证要求→连接证据与结论→检查正反两种情况均保留。

S340.reference: After the final round, both teams will reflect on which arguments were most convincing.
S340.explanation:
读懂：最后一轮后，两队会讨论哪些论证最有说服力。
解析：三块是“结束后／两队反思／最有力论证”；which 后使用陈述语序。
下次：听到复盘安排→连记参与者与评价对象→核对 both 和最高程度。

S341.reference: Coats go on the long rail.
S341.explanation:
读懂：外套挂在长衣架杆上；rail 指挂衣服的横杆。
解析：记“外套／长杆上”；long 限定哪根杆。
下次：听到物品分区→配对衣物与位置→核对 on 和 long。

S342.reference: Fold the scarves, then put them in this basket.
S342.explanation:
读懂：把围巾叠好，再放进这个篮子。
解析：先折叠，再放入篮子；scarves 是围巾的复数，them 回指这些围巾。
下次：听到收纳动作→依次记整理与存放→核对代词及容器。

S343.reference: Arrange the shirts by size so visitors can find them more easily.
S343.explanation:
读懂：按尺码排列衬衫，便于来访者找到。
解析：by size 是分类标准，so 引出目的；them 回指衬衫。
下次：听到分类→配对标准与物品→核对目的和代词。

S344.reference: An item without a label should stay on the table until we check it.
S344.explanation:
读懂：没有标签的衣物先留在桌上，等核查后再处理。
解析：按“无标签衣物／留桌上／直到核查”记；without 限定适用物品。
下次：听到暂存要求→记对象条件与终点→核对 without 和 until。

S345.reference: Small repairs are possible, but please ask before promising that something can be fixed.
S345.explanation:
读懂：小修补可以做，但承诺能修好之前先询问。
解析：可小修不等于所有东西都保证修好；before 连接询问与承诺顺序。
下次：听到能力及限制→分别记可做事项和确认要求→核对被动。

S346.reference: Clothes left after the event will be offered to the campus drama group.
S346.explanation:
读懂：活动后剩下的衣服会提供给校园戏剧社。
解析：长主语是“活动后留下的衣服”；will be offered 表示将被提供。
下次：听到剩余物品去向→先定对象范围→核对接收者和将来被动。

S347.reference: Keep the empty boxes for packing.
S347.explanation:
读懂：保留空箱子供打包使用。
解析：empty 限定箱子状态，for packing 给保留用途。
下次：听到保留物品→连记状态和目的→核对 for。

S348.explanation:
读懂：作品提交在周五晚上截止；Entries 指参赛提交。
解析：记“投稿截止／周五晚”；on 连接具体哪一天。
下次：听到截止安排→配对事项与日期时段→核对介词。

S349.reference: Give each photograph a short title.
S349.explanation:
读懂：给每张照片取个简短标题。
解析：each photograph 强调每一张；short 限定标题长度。
下次：听到逐件要求→配对对象与所需内容→核对 each。

S350.reference: You may submit three images, but only one can receive the main prize.
S350.explanation:
读懂：最多可提交三张图，但只有一张能获主要奖项。
解析：three 与 one 对应提交和获奖两种数量；but 表示限制关系。
下次：听到两个数量→分别配对动作→核对 only 的限制。

S351.reference: The description should explain where the picture was taken and why you chose it.
S351.explanation:
读懂：说明需交代拍摄地点和选择该照片的原因。
解析：where 与 why 并列两项信息；was taken 是照片被拍摄。
下次：听到说明要求→记地点和理由两栏→检查被动与代词。

S352.reference: If another person can be recognized, obtain their permission before entering the photograph.
S352.explanation:
读懂：照片中能辨认出他人时，参赛前先取得对方许可。
解析：按“可认出他人／取得其许可／提交前”记；their 指可辨认的人。
下次：听到提交条件→连接触发对象与事前要求→核对指代。

S353.reference: The judges will see the images without knowing which student submitted them.
S353.explanation:
读懂：评委查看图片时，不知道是哪位学生提交的。
解析：without knowing 说明评审时不具备的信息；them 回指图像。
下次：听到评审方式→记可见内容与隐藏信息→核对 which 后语序。

S354.reference: You can replace an entry before the deadline, provided that the new file keeps the same title.
S354.explanation:
读懂：截止前可以替换作品，但新文件须保留同一标题。
解析：三个约束是“可替换／截止前／同标题”；provided that 表示前提条件。
下次：听到带条件的修改→分记时限和一致要求→核对两个条件都在。

S355.reference: The demonstration table is up front.
S355.explanation:
读懂：演示台在前面；demonstration 是“演示”。
解析：记“演示台／前面”；up front 是位置整体。
下次：听到设备位置→配对对象和方位→核对完整位置短语。

S356.reference: Leave some space around the table.
S356.explanation:
读懂：在台子周围留些空位。
解析：动作是留空间，around 指周围而非台面上。
下次：听到场地要求→记所留空间的位置→核对 around。

S357.reference: Write down what you expect to happen before I release the ball.
S357.explanation:
读懂：我放开球前，先写下你预计会发生什么。
解析：先预测，再放球；what 引出预期内容，I 是释放球的人。
下次：听到预测任务→连接写下内容与观察起点→核对动作执行者。

S358.reference: Watch the point where the ball first touches the curved surface.
S358.explanation:
读懂：观察球第一次碰到曲面的位置。
解析：按“观察接触点／球首次接触／曲面”记；first 限定接触次数。
下次：听到观察对象→定位哪次事件及所在位置→核对 first。

S359.reference: What actually happens may differ from the prediction you made a moment ago.
S359.explanation:
读懂：实际发生的情况可能与刚才的预测不同。
解析：主语为“实际发生的事”；may differ from 保留可能不同及比较对象。
下次：听到结果比较→配对实际与预测→核对 may 和 from。

S360.reference: We will repeat the movement slowly so everyone can observe the part they missed.
S360.explanation:
读懂：会慢慢重做动作，让大家看到刚才漏掉的部分。
解析：按“慢速重复／大家观察／漏看部分”分块；they 回指观众。
下次：听到重复观察→连记方式、目的和目标部分→核对 slowly。

S361.reference: Please describe your observation before offering an explanation.
S361.explanation:
读懂：先描述观察到的现象，再提出解释。
解析：两项工作分别是描述与解释；before 规定先后。
下次：听到两种报告任务→先陈述所见再讲原因→核对顺序词。

S362.explanation:
读懂：洗衣房在楼下；laundry 指洗衣事务。
解析：记“洗衣房／楼下”，is 连接设施与位置。
下次：听到设施位置→配对地点与方向→检查 downstairs。

S363.reference: You need your residence card here.
S363.explanation:
读懂：这里需要用住宿卡。
解析：按“需要／你的住宿卡／这里”记，your 指本人证件。
下次：听到使用条件→连记所需物品与场所→核对 your。

S364.reference: A green light means the machine has finished its current cycle.
S364.explanation:
读懂：绿灯表示机器已完成当前洗涤程序。
解析：信号与完成状态对应；has finished 与 current cycle 一起记。
下次：听到信号解释→配对颜色和设备状态→核对完成结构。

S365.reference: Check inside the drum before adding your clothes to an empty machine.
S365.explanation:
读懂：向空机里放衣服前，先检查滚筒内部；drum 是“滚筒”。
解析：先看内部再放衣；inside 限定检查位置，empty 限定机器状态。
下次：听到使用前检查→连接位置与后续动作→核对 before。

S366.reference: If a machine stops unexpectedly, note its number and contact the residence office.
S366.explanation:
读懂：机器意外停止时，记下机号并联系住宿办公室。
解析：按“意外停止／记编号／联系办公室”记；its 回指停下的机器。
下次：听到故障处理→分记条件和两项动作→核对编号归属。

S367.reference: Clothes left in a machine after the cycle ends can be placed in the labeled basket.
S367.explanation:
读懂：洗涤程序结束后仍留在机器里的衣服，可放入有标签的篮子。
解析：先记“洗完仍留机内的衣服”，再接“可放标签篮”；after 限定时间，can be placed 是被动许可。
下次：听到长主语与处理办法→分记物品状态和新位置→核对时间限定与被动。

S368.reference: Remember to take all your belongings.
S368.explanation:
读懂：记得带走全部个人物品。
解析：remember to take 指别忘了要做的动作；all 保留全部范围。
下次：听到离开提醒→连接待做动作与物品范围→核对 all。

S369.explanation:
读懂：扫描工作台准备好了；scanning 是“扫描”。
解析：记“扫描台／准备好”；Our 表示本组的设备。
下次：听到工作准备→配对设备与状态→核对所属词。

S370.reference: Handle each photograph by its edges.
S370.explanation:
读懂：拿照片时抓边缘；edges 指“边”。
解析：each 限定逐张处理，its 回指该照片；by 指拿握位置。
下次：听到材料处理→配对对象和接触部位→核对 by。

S371.reference: Keep the original order even when several pictures seem almost identical.
S371.explanation:
读懂：即使多张照片看起来几乎一样，也要保持原顺序。
解析：让步连接外观相似与仍需保持的次序；almost 限定并非完全相同。
下次：听到排列要求→记保留项目和特殊情况→核对 original 与 almost。

S372.reference: The number on the envelope should appear at the beginning of each file name.
S372.explanation:
读懂：信封号码应放在每个文件名开头。
解析：按“信封编号／文件名开头／每个”记；两个位置分别指来源和记录位置。
下次：听到命名规则→配对取值来源与写入位置→核对 each。

S373.reference: If the date is uncertain, leave that field blank rather than guessing.
S373.explanation:
读懂：日期不确定时，日期栏留空，不要猜填。
解析：条件为不确定；rather than 对照留空与猜测，that field 指日期栏。
下次：听到未知信息→连接不确定条件与处理方法→核对排除动作。

S374.reference: A second volunteer will compare the digital image with the original before it is saved.
S374.explanation:
读懂：保存数字图像前，另一位志愿者会把它与原照片核对。
解析：按“另一人核对／数字件与原件／保存前”记；it 指待保存的数字图像。
下次：听到质量复核→连记核对者、两份材料和时点→检查指代。

S375.reference: When you finish a folder, record how many images were added and which photographs still need attention.
S375.explanation:
读懂：处理完一夹后，记录新增图数及哪些照片仍需处理。
解析：有“完成时机／新增数量／待处理照片”三块；how many 与 which 引出不同待记信息。
下次：听到交接记录→分清完成数量与遗留对象→核对两项记录都保留。

S376.reference: I remember preparing a full dinner for my family without anyone helping me. The meal was simple, but I had to plan the shopping and make sure everything was ready at the same time. It mattered because I usually depended on other people in the kitchen. After that evening, cooking felt less intimidating, and I started preparing meals more often. The achievement was small, but it changed what I believed I could do independently.
S376.explanation:
读懂：讲一项记得清楚的小成就，并解释它为什么对你重要；achievement 是“成就”。
解析：示例把独立做饭与信心变化连接起来，既说完成了什么，也解释个人意义。其他学习或生活进步同样可以，不必讲重大获奖。
下次：听到 achievement 和 why→选一个具体完成的事情→补它带来的变化，检查事件与意义都有表达。

S377.reference: I keep a short notebook instead of trying to save every photograph I take. After an important day, I write down one detail that I would otherwise forget. For example, after my first presentation, I recorded a classmate's encouraging comment. That sentence brings back the feeling of the day more clearly than a picture of the classroom would. The notebook is easy to maintain because each entry only takes a few minutes.
S377.explanation:
读懂：说明你怎样保存重要经历，并举例；keep a record 指“留下记录”。
解析：参考先给记笔记这一方法，再用演讲后的鼓励话说明记录内容与作用。照片或其他方式也可，关键是方法后有具体实例。
下次：听到记录方法题→先说采用的方式→用一次经历说明实际留下什么，检查例子是否支撑该方法。

S378.reference: I think small celebrations can help people stay motivated. Working toward a difficult goal may take months, so noticing progress gives people a reason to continue. My study group sometimes takes a short walk together after finishing a major assignment. We enjoy the break, but we do not spend more time planning the celebration than doing the work. For me, the benefit depends on keeping the celebration proportional to the achievement.
S378.explanation:
读懂：判断庆祝能否维持动力，还是可能分散对工作的注意；motivated 是“有动力的”。
解析：示例支持适度庆祝，用长期目标和小组短暂休息解释作用，并加上规模应适当的条件。支持另一面也成立，需解释庆祝如何影响工作。
下次：听到作用的两种可能→明确自己的判断→给一个因果和例子，检查是否说明适用条件而非只喊口号。

S379.reference: It should consider how much people have improved, not just who already performs best. Someone who began with little experience may have made remarkable progress even if their final result is not the strongest. I would also look at whether their work helped other members. These criteria should be explained before the decision. That way, recognition can encourage learning and cooperation instead of making the same small group seem permanently more valuable than everyone else.
S379.explanation:
读懂：组织每年只能表彰少数成员，选择时应考虑什么；recognize 在这里指“认可、表彰”。
解析：参考用进步幅度与对他人的帮助提出标准，再说明公开标准的意义。题目允许不同标准，不要求照搬示例的两项或否定最终表现。
下次：听到名额有限的选择题→提出能区分候选人的标准→解释标准服务的目的，检查是否回答了如何选择。

S380.reference: I usually look at a map before I start walking, but I do not watch it continuously. I try to remember one or two landmarks, such as a large park or a station entrance. Then I compare what I see with the general direction on the map. This approach helps me notice the neighborhood instead of concentrating only on my phone. If I become uncertain, I stop somewhere convenient and check the route again.
S380.explanation:
读懂：说明到陌生街区后通常怎样辨路；unfamiliar 是“不熟悉的”。
解析：示例按出发前看图、途中记地标、不确定时再查的顺序回答，说明方法如何帮助辨路。问路等其他习惯也可以。
下次：听到 usually 和做法→按实际先后讲两三步→说明关键一步的作用，检查回答没有变成地点介绍。

S381.reference: One weekend, I walked through an area near my college without choosing a destination. I noticed music coming from a small community hall and found that a group was rehearsing a public concert. A volunteer invited visitors to listen quietly at the back. I stayed for half an hour and later returned for the performance. Without that unplanned walk, I probably would never have learned that the group existed so close to campus.
S381.explanation:
读懂：讲一次没有详细计划的探索，以及它带来的有趣发现；discovery 是“发现”。
解析：参考连接随意散步、听到音乐、进入礼堂和后来再去的结果，明确发现如何发生。自己的普通街区经历也足够，不必是远途旅行。
下次：听到一次意外发现→先交代为何没有详细计划→讲触发发现的线索和结果，检查发现与探索有联系。

S382.reference: Generally, they do. A visitor can check routes and travel times without needing someone else to guide every step. However, independence also means being able to respond when the suggested route is unsuitable. I think people benefit most when they use a digital map to understand the area, rather than following instructions without looking around. For example, noticing nearby landmarks can help them continue even if their phone battery becomes low.
S382.explanation:
读懂：评价电子地图是否让人在陌生地方更独立；independent 指“不依赖别人”。
解析：示例先肯定获取路线的便利，再把独立扩展到路线不适合时能自行应对。也可以持否定观点，但需解释地图使用怎样改变依赖程度。
下次：听到工具是否提升能力→明确能力的含义→讲工具带来的作用及一个限制，检查因果紧扣独立性。

S383.reference: I would spend the afternoon in one neighborhood. Moving between several famous places could take up much of the limited time, especially in a large city. Staying in one area would let me walk slowly, visit a local shop, and observe everyday life. I might miss some well-known sights, but I would remember the experience more clearly. This choice would be different if there were one particular landmark I had wanted to see for years.
S383.explanation:
读懂：one free afternoon（只有一个空闲下午）是限制；比较看多个名胜与深入一个街区，并说明理由。
解析：参考把时间限制与交通、体验深度相连，并承认可能错过名胜。另一种选择也可成立，重点是理由回应有限时段，而非泛谈城市好坏。
下次：听到有限时间的两种安排→先选主要方案→解释时间如何影响收益，检查是否承认合理的取舍。

S384.reference: I once brought an old version of my slides to a group presentation. The main ideas were there, but several corrections were missing, and my teammates had to explain them. Afterward, I began putting the date in every file name and checking the final version before leaving home. The mistake did not ruin the presentation, but it taught me that preparing good work and bringing the correct copy are two separate responsibilities.
S384.explanation:
读懂：描述一次小错误及从中得到的教训；lesson 在这里指“经验教训”。
解析：示例说明拿错版本、造成什么影响和后来改变的具体做法，教训由事件直接产生。其他小失误也可，不能只笼统说以后会更小心。
下次：听到 mistake 和 lesson→用一句交代错误→讲一项因此改变的行为，检查教训是否具体可执行。

S385.reference: I try to understand the comment before defending what I did. If the mistake is clear, I thank the person and correct it. If I am unsure, I ask them to show me the part they mean. For example, when a classmate questions a calculation, we can check the steps together. I do not always enjoy being corrected immediately, but asking for a specific example helps me focus on the work instead of taking the comment personally.
S385.explanation:
读懂：说明别人指出你工作中的错误时，你通常怎样回应；points out 是“指出”。
解析：参考先听懂，再根据清楚或不确定两种情况采取行动，计算的例子说明如何落实。题目不要求假装从不难受，仍需交代实际回应。
下次：听到他人反馈后的反应→先讲你的处理步骤→用一个小例子说明，检查重点在行动而非只谈情绪。

S386.reference: Yes, when learners have enough information to find the problem themselves. Searching for an error can make them examine the reasoning behind an answer, which may be more useful than simply copying a correction. A teacher could point to the relevant step or ask a guiding question. However, if a student keeps repeating the same misunderstanding and cannot move forward, direct explanation is helpful. The aim should be learning, not making students struggle for as long as possible.
S386.explanation:
读懂：评价教师是否有时应让学生自行发现错误，而非立即纠正；sometimes 表示只问部分情况。
解析：示例支持有条件地自行查错，说明理解推理的好处，并提出需要直接解释的边界。不能把题干的有时扩大成所有错误都放任不管。
下次：听到 sometimes 的教育判断→保留部分情境的范围→说明益处和适用条件，检查没有绝对化。

S387.reference: I would begin by examining how the group worked. A mistake that appears to belong to one person may also reflect unclear instructions or a missing review step. For example, two members might prepare different versions because nobody agreed on a shared file. Understanding that process helps prevent the problem from happening again. Individuals should still take responsibility for their actions, but naming someone without changing the working method may leave the group with exactly the same risk next time.
S387.explanation:
读懂：how the group worked（团队如何合作）是一个检查方向；比较它与找出谁犯错，哪种更有用。
解析：参考选择先查流程，用共享文件的例子解释预防重复问题，同时保留个人责任。其他侧重也可，只要说明它如何帮助解决团队问题。
下次：听到两种复盘重点→确定先处理哪一项→用问题成因与改进结果连接理由，检查没有偷换成完全免除责任。

S388.reference: I usually take a walk or read something I already have with me. I do not immediately fill the hour with another appointment, because finding a replacement activity can take more effort than it is worth. If I am near home, I might cook a simple meal. The important thing for me is choosing something that fits the available time without creating a new obligation.
S388.explanation:
读懂：说临时空出一小时时通常做什么；canceled 指“被取消”。
解析：示例先说活动，再解释为何选容易开始的事；也可选完成待办，需与一小时相配。
下次：听到临时空闲→选一种通常做法→用时间限制解释选择，检查是否回答具体活动。

S389.reference: A lecture was once delayed for half an hour, so I stayed outside with a classmate instead of opening my notes again. We talked about a project that had been bothering me. Saying the problem aloud helped me notice a simpler way to divide the work. I had expected the delay to waste my time, but the conversation made the rest of the afternoon easier.
S389.explanation:
读懂：讲一次意外休息为何有用；unplanned 是“未预先安排的”。
解析：参考从讲座延迟讲到交谈帮助拆解任务，益处与这段空闲有因果联系。
下次：听到经历及效果→先交代空闲如何出现→讲其中一件事及结果，检查联系清楚。

S390.reference: No. Rest can matter even when it does not produce something that can be counted or displayed. After a busy day, sitting quietly may help someone return to other activities with more patience. I also enjoy doing things simply because they are pleasant. Of course, responsibilities cannot always wait, but treating every spare moment as another assignment could make free time feel like work.
S390.explanation:
读懂：评价每段空闲是否都必须有产出；productive 指“有成效的”。
解析：示例区分休息价值与可量化产出，同时保留责任限制；支持有计划利用也可。
下次：听到 every 的绝对范围→明确是否接受→用理由和情境限定，检查没有只列活动。

S391.reference: I would leave a short period unplanned while keeping the main meeting times clear. Members may want different things from the trip, such as taking photographs or talking over lunch. A little choice can make the day feel more personal. However, the free period should have a clear ending and meeting place, so the people who prefer structure do not spend it worrying about missing the group.
S391.explanation:
读懂：比较社团一日游保留空档与安排全天；throughout 表示“贯穿”。
解析：参考选择留空档，说明个人选择的好处与集合安排；排满也可，需解释群体需要。
下次：听到团体日程选择→确定主方案→连接参与者差异与集合约束，检查理由服务该行程。

S392.reference: My younger cousin showed me a useful way to organize photographs on my phone. I had been looking for pictures one at a time, while she used folders for different events. She explained the steps and then asked me to try them myself. It was a small lesson, but I still use that system. It reminded me that useful knowledge does not always follow age.
S392.explanation:
读懂：much older or younger（年长或年幼很多）限定学习对象；讲向这样的人学到的一件事。
解析：示例明确谁教了什么、怎样学会及持续用途；普通技能也足够，不必是重大人生建议。
下次：听到跨年龄学习→选具体技能→补学习过程和使用结果，检查人物关系清楚。

S393.reference: A shared activity helps me most. If we are cooking or working on a puzzle, we already have something concrete to discuss, so I do not feel pressure to invent an impressive topic. I also ask about the person's own experience instead of assuming that everyone their age thinks alike. Once we have exchanged a few stories, the age difference usually feels less important to me.
S393.explanation:
读懂：说明什么能帮助你自在地跨代交流；generation 指“一代人”。
解析：参考用共同活动和询问个人经历说明做法，不把年龄当作固定性格。
下次：听到交流困难→提出一项可执行做法→解释它如何打开话题，检查不是泛说要尊重。

S394.reference: Yes, because people gain experience in different areas. An older neighbor might teach a student how to care for a particular plant, while the student helps the neighbor edit a short video. Neither person has to be the expert in everything. When both have something to contribute, the relationship can feel more equal, and asking for help may become easier for each of them.
S394.explanation:
读懂：评价跨代学习是否应双向，并举例；both directions 指“双方互相学习”。
解析：示例给出两项相反方向的帮助，再解释关系上的作用；例子是可能情形，不是年龄通则。
下次：听到双向及例子→分别交代双方贡献→说明互学益处，检查两个方向都有。

S395.reference: I would suggest making a small exhibition about the neighborhood. Residents could contribute photographs, memories, drawings, or recorded descriptions. These tasks allow different interests and abilities to matter without assigning roles purely by age. The shared exhibition would also give people a reason to meet more than once. I would begin with a small group, so everyone had time to explain what they wanted to include.
S395.explanation:
读懂：bring younger and older residents together（让年轻与年长居民聚在一起）是目标；建议活动并解释原因。
解析：参考提出社区小展览，把多种贡献方式与持续交流联系起来；其他活动亦可。
下次：听到活动建议→提出具体共同产物或目标→解释不同参与者如何加入，检查可执行性。

S396.reference: I write the promise in the same calendar that I use for classes and appointments. If it involves a small task, I add a specific time to do it rather than leaving it on a general list. For example, I might schedule ten minutes to send a classmate my notes. Seeing the promise beside my other plans reminds me that another person is depending on it.
S396.explanation:
读懂：说明如何记住对别人的承诺；promise 是“承诺”。
解析：示例给出记录方法和具体安排，解释为什么比泛泛记着更有帮助；方法可不同。
下次：听到记忆承诺→讲工具或行动→加一个使用例子，检查怎样避免遗忘。

S397.reference: I once agreed to help a friend move some books on Saturday, but on Thursday I learned that I had to attend a class meeting that Saturday morning. I contacted my friend as soon as I found out and offered to help on Friday evening instead. That time worked for both of us. The change was inconvenient, but explaining it early gave my friend a real choice instead of a last-minute surprise.
S397.explanation:
读懂：involved another person（涉及另一个人）限定计划；讲必须修改这种计划时怎样处理。
解析：参考包含变更原因、及时联系和替代方案；不用证明自己毫无责任，重点是处理过程。
下次：听到改约经历→说明冲突→讲沟通与结果，检查另一人的安排也被考虑。

S398.reference: I prefer making fewer promises that I can realistically keep. Saying yes can feel generous at first, but it is not helpful if several people later discover that I cannot do what I offered. I can still be supportive by suggesting another person or giving a smaller amount of help. For me, a clear limit is often more useful than an enthusiastic answer that creates false expectations.
S398.explanation:
读懂：fewer promises（较少的承诺）与尽可能答应帮助形成两种选择；比较并解释。
解析：参考将可靠性与他人预期连接，并给出有限帮助的替代方式；选择另一边需说明怎样落实。
下次：听到两种帮助态度→选主原则→解释对受助者的实际影响，检查不是只有价值判断。

S399.reference: The group should first ask what is preventing the person from finishing and make the next task very clear. A smaller assignment with an earlier check-in could show whether support or a different role helps. At the same time, the group needs a backup plan so everyone else's work is protected. If the problem continues, responsibilities may need to change, with the reasons explained directly to the member.
S399.explanation:
读懂：处理反复误期，同时保留公平机会；repeatedly 表示“多次”。
解析：参考兼顾了解原因、可检验的改进机会与其他成员进度；不要求唯一处分方式。
下次：听到公平与效率双重要求→分别安排支持和边界→说明后续条件，检查两方利益都回应。

S400.reference: I enjoy stories in which an ordinary person has to make a difficult choice. The setting does not need to be unusual. I become interested when I can understand two possible decisions and wonder which one the character will make. A mystery can work that way, but so can a story about friendship. I usually remember the character's reasons longer than the details of the plot.
S400.explanation:
读懂：说明喜欢的故事类型及吸引点；character 指“人物”。
解析：示例把普通人的选择作为偏好，再解释期待如何形成；无需列具体书名。
下次：听到偏好及原因→先概括类型→说一个吸引你的特点，检查原因与类型相关。

S401.reference: In a film I watched, a student seemed unfriendly because she kept leaving group activities early. Later, the story showed that she was going home to look after a younger brother. I began to understand her behavior differently. She had not changed, but the information available to me had. That experience made the character more interesting than someone who was clearly kind or unkind from the beginning.
S401.explanation:
读懂：changed your opinion（改变了你的看法）是重点；说明故事发展中什么改变了你对人物的判断。
解析：参考明确初始判断、新信息与新理解；人物本身不必改变，观众的信息也会改变评价。
下次：听到看法变化→依次讲原判断、触发线索、新判断→检查转变原因。

S402.reference: I prefer an ending that resolves the main problem but leaves a few smaller questions open. I want to feel that following the story has led somewhere, especially if the characters have faced a difficult decision. However, knowing every detail of their future can make the story less interesting to discuss. Some uncertainty gives me room to imagine what the characters might do after the final scene.
S402.explanation:
读懂：比较明确结局与保留悬念；unanswered 指“未获解答的”。
解析：示例提出分层偏好：主要问题解决、小问题开放；不强迫二选一到绝对程度。
下次：听到结局偏好→明确最在意的部分→用阅读体验解释，检查没有只复述两项。

S403.reference: For a new group, I would choose the familiar story first. Members could concentrate on listening to different interpretations rather than worrying about whether they understood the basic plot. Familiar material does not mean the discussion will be simple; people may notice quite different details. Once everyone feels comfortable contributing, I would suggest the unfamiliar story as a way to explore something new together.
S403.explanation:
读懂：familiar popular story（熟悉的热门故事）与陌生较难的故事是两个选项；为讨论组作选择。
解析：参考把选择与新组成员参与连接，解释熟悉材料也能讨论深入；其他选择同样可论证。
下次：听到材料选择→确定小组当前需要→连接材料特点与参与效果，检查理由回应讨论场景。

S404.reference: I usually ask for a small example. An explanation can sound clear at first while still leaving me unsure how to use the idea. If the speaker applies it to one concrete situation, I can see where my understanding stops. Sometimes I also repeat what I think the explanation means and ask whether I have understood correctly. That gives the speaker a more specific problem to address.
S404.explanation:
读懂：do not understand（没听懂）是追问的起点；说明通常请说话者怎样帮助你。
解析：参考用要例子和复述理解两种做法说明如何定位困惑；不必同时采用两种。
下次：听到理解困难→选一种追问方法→解释它暴露什么缺口，检查行动具体。

S405.reference: I was planning a presentation with far too many slides when a friend asked what I wanted the audience to remember the next day. I had been thinking only about including all the information I had found. Her question shifted my attention to the audience's needs. I chose one main point and removed several sections. The presentation became shorter, but its purpose was much easier to explain.
S405.explanation:
读懂：see a problem differently（换个角度看问题）是结果；讲别人一个问题怎样带来这种变化。
解析：示例说明原先关注信息量、提问后关注观众记忆，变化具体可见。
下次：听到启发性问题→给出问题内容→对照前后想法，检查变化由该问题引起。

S406.reference: It can feel embarrassing, but I think it is often helpful. Other people may have the same uncertainty and be waiting for someone else to mention it. A basic question can also reveal that the group is using an important word in different ways. I would ask briefly and connect the question to the current task. That makes it easier for everyone to see why clarification matters.
S406.explanation:
读懂：a basic question（一个基础问题）是讨论对象；评价在群体中提问的帮助与尴尬。
解析：参考承认尴尬感，再解释澄清共同概念的好处；题目允许不同体验。
下次：听到感受与效果→分别说明两者→用具体情境支持主判断，检查不是只说别害怕。

S407.reference: A teacher could pause at a few planned points and invite questions about the main idea just covered. Questions that require a separate discussion could go on a visible list for later. Students would know that their questions were taken seriously, even when they could not be answered immediately. The teacher should actually return to that list, because repeatedly postponing questions without following up would discourage participation.
S407.explanation:
读懂：兼顾鼓励提问与课堂不跑题；focus 指“重点”。
解析：参考安排提问时点、暂存偏题问题和后续回应，两个要求都被照顾；方法可替换。
下次：听到两种需要→给各自安排具体措施→补衔接方式，检查方案不是只限制提问。

S408.reference: At home, we put shared keys in the same bowl by the door. It is a simple rule, but it saves everyone from searching through different rooms when they are about to leave. Nobody has to remember who used the keys last. I like the rule because its purpose is obvious and following it takes only a few seconds, so it is easy to maintain.
S408.explanation:
读懂：everyday rule（日常规则）限定范围；说一条有用的规则并解释帮助。
解析：示例用钥匙固定归位说明省时与易遵守；普通家庭规则即可。
下次：听到规则及作用→讲清具体行为→给一个避免的问题，检查帮助能从规则推出。

S409.reference: My study group normally met in person, but one week I had to be away from campus. I asked whether I could join by video and offered to send my part of the work in advance. The group agreed because everyone could still discuss the same material. I appreciated the exception, and I made sure it did not leave the others with extra preparation at the last minute.
S409.explanation:
读懂：讲需要一次例外的经历；exception 是“不按通常规则处理的情况”。
解析：参考说明规则、原因、替代安排和结果；不要求把所有例外都描述成合理。
下次：听到例外经历→交代通常做法→讲为何调整及如何补足目的，检查结果明确。

S410.reference: Not always. A rule is meant to serve a purpose, and an unusual situation may require a different action to achieve that purpose. For example, a quiet study room might allow a brief spoken request for help. However, people should be careful about treating personal convenience as a special case. I would consider the effect on others and explain the exception when possible.
S410.explanation:
读懂：评价认同目的是否就必须在所有情境严格照做；always 是“总是”。
解析：参考用安静区短暂求助说明目的与字面执行可能不同，并保留对他人影响的边界。
下次：听到 always→检验特殊情境→连接规则目的和实际后果，检查未把例外扩大成随意违反。

S411.reference: The club should explain the kinds of circumstances it can consider and use the same process for everyone. Members should not need a personal friendship with the organizer to ask. Individual details may remain private, but the general reasons for the policy can be public. I would also review whether repeated exceptions show that the original rule needs changing, rather than continually making separate decisions that seem inconsistent.
S411.explanation:
读懂：treated unequally（被不平等对待）是需要避免的感受；说明社团怎样兼顾出勤例外与公平。
解析：参考区分公开流程与私人细节，并提出反复例外时复查规则；不是必须公开个人原因。
下次：听到灵活与公平→设计一致申请流程→说明隐私及复查边界，检查两方面都回应。

S412.reference: I feel restless because I keep imagining several possible outcomes. It helps me to separate what I can prepare from what I cannot decide yet. For example, while waiting to hear whether a club event is approved, I can collect ideas without buying materials. Having a small useful task makes the waiting easier, and it prevents me from checking for news every few minutes.
S412.explanation:
读懂：waiting for a decision（等待决定）是情境；说明决定影响自己计划时的感受。
解析：参考先说不安，再用可做准备说明应对；可以有其他情绪，不必照搬积极结尾。
下次：听到等待感受→先直接说情绪→用一项行为或例子解释，检查没有只讲最终结果。

S413.reference: We planned to draw buildings outdoors for an art club meeting, but heavy rain was possible. One member arranged permission for us to sketch inside a large hall if necessary. When the rain started, we moved there instead of canceling the meeting. The drawings were different from what we had expected, but we still practiced together. The backup plan protected the purpose of the activity rather than every original detail.
S413.explanation:
读懂：讲备用方案起作用的经历；backup plan 是“备选计划”。
解析：示例交代下雨风险、室内备选及仍能画画的结果；核心是备选如何保留活动目的。
下次：听到备用方案→说触发情境→连接替代行动和保留的目标，检查作用具体。

S414.reference: It depends on what can go wrong and whether the decision can be changed. For a small hobby project, starting may teach me more than waiting for perfect information. I can try it for a short time and then decide whether to continue. For an activity involving many people or a large commitment, I would want clearer information first. The amount of preparation should match the consequences.
S414.explanation:
读懂：评价开始新活动前是否应等情况更确定；certainty 是“确定性”。
解析：参考用后果大小及可调整性区分情况，不把谨慎或立即行动设成绝对原则。
下次：听到是否等待→先判断后果和可逆性→给相应条件与例子，检查不是空泛说看情况。

S415.reference: I would ask members for the dates they already know are impossible and choose from the remaining options. The team should set a clear point when the date becomes final, so planning can continue. It could also offer another way to contribute for anyone who later cannot attend. This will not satisfy everyone perfectly, but it makes the decision understandable and keeps one unknown schedule from delaying the whole event.
S415.explanation:
读懂：before all members know their schedules（所有人日程尚未确定时）是限制；建议怎样选活动日期。
解析：参考收集已知限制、设定确定时点并安排替代参与，回应必须先决策的条件。
下次：听到信息不全又需行动→利用已知约束→给确定期限与补救，检查方案能形成决定。

S416.reference: I keep tickets from places I have visited with friends. They are small and usually have a date or a location printed on them, so they help me remember particular days. The tickets are not valuable to anyone else, and I do not try to collect every possible kind. I simply keep the ones connected with an experience that I would like to remember.
S416.explanation:
读懂：keep or collect（保存或收集）是题目所问的习惯；说明物品种类与兴趣来源。
解析：示例选择普通票根，以记忆价值解释兴趣；不要求收藏品昂贵或成套。
下次：听到收藏偏好→明确物品→连接一个个人意义，检查不是只列名称。

S417.reference: I ask whether the object reminds me of something specific or is simply something I am used to seeing. If several objects represent the same event, I usually keep one and photograph the others. That is not a perfect substitute, but it helps me use the space I have. I also leave a little room for future memories instead of treating the current collection as finished forever.
S417.explanation:
读懂：limited space（有限空间）是限制；说明怎样决定保留哪些物品。
解析：参考提出特定记忆与重复代表物两项判断；拍照只是可选办法，不要求抛弃实物。
下次：听到筛选限制→给可应用的标准→说明一次取舍，检查标准回应空间不足。

S418.reference: Yes. Ordinary objects can show a pattern that is difficult to notice when we see them separately. A collection of local shop bags, for example, might show different designs or changes in the names of businesses. The collector's explanation matters too, because visitors may not know why the objects were chosen. A collection can become interesting through the relationships between its parts, not only through rare individual pieces.
S418.explanation:
读懂：ordinary（普通的）限定收藏品；评价这样的个人收藏是否仍能教会别人一些东西。
解析：示例从并置后看到变化与收藏者解释两点展开；所举购物袋只是可能例子。
下次：听到普通物品价值→寻找物件间的关系→用实例说明学到什么，检查不是只说有趣。

S419.reference: I would group them by stories, such as journeys, friendships, or learning a skill. That could bring very different objects together and give visitors a reason to compare them. A ticket beside a drawing might be more surprising than a row of similar tickets. I would still add clear labels identifying each object, so the arrangement did not become confusing for people who had not met the collectors.
S419.explanation:
读懂：by type（按类别）与按背后故事是两种分组法；为个人收藏展选择并解释。
解析：参考按故事分组，说明比较收益并用标签保持清楚；按类别也可支持。
下次：听到展览组织方式→选择主线→解释参观者如何理解，检查安排与目的相连。

S420.reference: I would explain a few practical things before the gathering starts, such as where to sit and how the activity usually works. I would also introduce the guest to one person who shares an interest with them. I would avoid making them the center of attention immediately. A small amount of information and one friendly conversation can be more welcoming than a long public introduction.
S420.explanation:
读懂：first-time guest（第一次来的客人）是帮助对象；说明怎样让他在惯常聚会中自在。
解析：参考用实用信息和单独介绍回应陌生感；不要求公开热烈欢迎。
下次：听到帮助新人→找其信息或社交困难→给具体动作，检查动作对应困难。

S421.reference: At my first drawing club meeting, I arrived after people had already started. A member quietly moved a chair beside her and showed me the materials everyone was using. She did not stop the meeting or ask me to introduce myself in front of the whole room. That simple action let me join naturally. Later, once I felt more comfortable, I began talking with the other members.
S421.explanation:
读懂：feel welcome（感到受欢迎）是结果；讲别人怎样帮助你融入陌生群体。
解析：示例用让座、介绍材料及后来交流交代具体帮助和结果；小动作也可成为完整经历。
下次：听到被欢迎的经历→选具体行动→说明它怎样改变感受或参与，检查因果明确。

S422.reference: Sometimes a small change is worthwhile, especially if the normal routine depends on knowledge the guest does not yet have. A short explanation or a slower first round can help without changing the whole activity. However, the guest may also enjoy seeing how the group normally works. I would ask what they need rather than assuming that making everything different is always the most welcoming choice.
S422.explanation:
读懂：usual routine（惯常安排）是可能改变的内容；评价是否值得为一位新客人调整。
解析：参考区分小幅帮助与全面改变，并考虑客人需要；不是所有变化都必需。
下次：听到是否调整惯例→识别实际障碍→说明调整范围与理由，检查没有替客人假定全部需求。

S423.reference: The host should make participation available without forcing it. They could explain that watching for a while is welcome and offer a small role if the guest later wants one. Pressure might make the guest concentrate on avoiding embarrassment instead of enjoying the activity. At the same time, the host should check in occasionally, because quiet observation does not always mean that the person wants to be left completely alone.
S423.explanation:
读懂：prefers to observe（更愿意旁观）是客人意愿；说明主人怎样兼顾它与参与目标。
解析：参考提供可选参与并适时关照，区分不强迫与完全不理；其他尊重意愿的方案也可。
下次：听到意愿冲突→保留选择权→给逐步参与的途径，检查双方目标都被理解。

S424.reference: I usually choose something familiar for myself, but I am happy to taste a small amount of a friend's dish if they offer. That way, I can enjoy the meal without worrying that I will dislike everything I ordered. Over time, those small tastes have introduced me to several foods I now choose regularly. I like exploring gradually rather than making every meal an experiment.
S424.explanation:
读懂：familiar food（熟悉的食物）与新食物形成选择；说明和朋友吃饭时的偏好及原因。
解析：参考选择熟悉主餐加少量尝试，用渐进探索解释；选完全尝新也可。
下次：听到饮食偏好→先说通常选择→用自身体验解释，检查不泛谈营养。

S425.reference: A classmate invited several of us to make dumplings at her apartment. While we worked, she explained that her family usually prepared them together before a celebration. I had known her mainly as a quiet person in class, but during the meal she enjoyed showing everyone what to do. The experience helped me see a more confident side of her and gave us something to talk about afterward.
S425.explanation:
读懂：learn something about another person（更了解另一个人）是结果；讲一顿饭怎样带来这种了解。
解析：参考通过共同做饭与对方表现建立新认识，不把一道菜当作整个文化的代表。
下次：听到饭与了解他人→描述互动→讲获得的新认识，检查两者有联系。

S426.reference: It is useful as a beginning, but it gives a limited picture by itself. A dish becomes more informative when someone explains when they eat it, who prepares it, and how different families make it. Otherwise, visitors may remember only whether they liked the taste. I would use a shared meal to start a conversation, while making clear that one person's food habits cannot represent everyone in a culture.
S426.explanation:
读懂：a limited picture（有限的呈现）提示范围；评价共享食物介绍文化的作用与局限。
解析：示例把食物当谈话起点，再说明个人习惯的代表性有限；可强调另一面但需解释。
下次：听到文化介绍方式→区分入口与全部认识→用具体信息说明边界，检查避免一概而论。

S427.reference: I would prefer many small dishes to sample. Trying different flavors would give visitors a natural reason to move around and speak to several people. A long explanation at every table might make the event feel like a lesson rather than a social gathering. I would still include short descriptions and let visitors ask questions, so people who wanted more detail could get it without slowing everyone else down.
S427.explanation:
读懂：explained in detail（详细讲解）对应少量菜肴；与多种试吃比较，选择活动形式并解释。
解析：参考支持多样试吃，把流动交流与活动目的相连，同时保留询问途径。
下次：听到活动形式比较→选主形式→说明参与体验怎样变化，检查理由对应活动目标。

S428.reference: I find it difficult to wait when a group cannot agree on a simple meeting time. I keep thinking that we could have made a decision much earlier. To avoid becoming impatient, I sometimes suggest two possible times and ask everyone to choose by a particular evening. Having a clear next step helps me more than repeatedly asking whether anyone has made up their mind yet.
S428.explanation:
读懂：difficult to be patient（难以保持耐心）是重点；举一种日常情境。
解析：参考先指出约时间，再用具体行动解释自己的反应；无需声称总能耐心。
下次：听到困难情境→给一个明确场景→说明为何难等或如何反应，检查不是泛谈性格。

S429.reference: I wanted to finish a drawing quickly, but my instructor suggested leaving it overnight before making the final changes. When I looked again the next day, I noticed that one part was much darker than the rest. I adjusted it and liked the result more. The extra time did not improve the drawing by itself; it gave me a fresh chance to judge what needed attention.
S429.explanation:
读懂：waiting longer（多等一段时间）是起因；讲它怎样带来更好的结果。
解析：示例说明隔夜再看如何发现具体问题，避免把等得久本身说成必然有益。
下次：听到等待收益→交代等待中改变了什么→连接实际改进，检查因果具体。

S430.reference: I would put speed first, provided that the service still does its job properly. Clear updates are helpful, but they do not replace actually solving the problem. If a desk regularly has a long queue, I would rather it change the way work is organized than add more signs explaining the delay. Once the process is reasonably efficient, honest information about the remaining wait becomes useful.
S430.explanation:
读懂：waiting process clear（等待过程清楚）与服务速度形成比较；说明哪项更重要。
解析：参考优先效率，解释通知不能替代解决问题；也可主张清晰度，须说明场景。
下次：听到服务优先级→选主要价值→解释其对使用者的影响，检查没有把另一项说成毫无用处。

S431.reference: The organizer could teach one basic version of the activity to everyone and then offer an optional extension. Beginners would have time to practice the foundation, while experienced members could attempt something more demanding. They could come together again to share what they tried. I would avoid asking the experienced members to act as helpers throughout the whole session, because they also joined in order to learn.
S431.explanation:
读懂：different speeds（不同速度）是组织难点；说明怎样同时照顾新手与熟练者。
解析：参考用共同基础加可选延伸回应两种学习需求，也说明不能总让熟手承担辅导。
下次：听到能力差异→设计共同部分与可选任务→检查双方都有学习机会。

S432.reference: Yes, especially short games where everyone starts with roughly the same chance. I enjoy a quick word game with friends because competition makes us concentrate and react faster. The result matters while we are playing, but it does not affect how we treat one another afterward. I am less interested in competitions that take a long time to prepare for or depend mainly on equipment someone can afford.
S432.explanation:
读懂：compete with one another（彼此竞争）限定活动类型；说是否喜欢并举例。
解析：示例给出短词语游戏和吸引点，同时限定偏好；不必喜欢所有形式的竞争。
下次：听到态度及例子→先表态→用一项活动解释体验，检查例子具体。

S433.reference: Several friends and I once made a short video for a club celebration. One person filmed, another edited, and I organized the interviews. We had different ideas about the style, but showing a rough version helped us decide what fitted together. I liked seeing parts that I could not have produced alone. The finished video felt like a shared achievement rather than a collection of separate contributions.
S433.explanation:
读懂：a shared result（共同的结果）是目标；讲与别人一起完成任务的经历。
解析：参考说明分工、协调方法和共同成果，合作过程可见；并非只列多人名字。
下次：听到合作经历→交代各自贡献→讲一次衔接及结果，检查共同目标明确。

S434.reference: It can, when the competition is between teams rather than between people who need to help one another. A team puzzle contest gives members a reason to share clues and divide tasks quickly. However, the group still needs to value everyone's contribution, including less visible work. If one person becomes concerned only with getting credit, the competition may weaken cooperation instead of improving it.
S434.explanation:
读懂：cooperate better（更好地合作）是可能的结果；评价竞争能否促进它。
解析：参考区别队际竞争与组内抢功，用拼图赛说明机制；可以持否定态度并举证。
下次：听到竞争影响合作→明确竞争发生在哪层→连接行为变化与结果，检查没有只说激励。

S435.reference: I would avoid competition at the first meeting. New members may not know the activity or one another, and an immediate ranking could make some people feel that they do not belong. I would begin with a shared challenge that has several possible roles. Once members feel comfortable, an optional contest could be enjoyable. Participation should come before proving who is already the most skilled.
S435.explanation:
读懂：encourage participation（鼓励参与）是目的；评价新社团是否应该用比赛实现它。
解析：参考按入门阶段选择先合作后可选竞赛，理由回应新成员归属感；比赛方案也可成立。
下次：听到招新活动选择→考虑参与者起点→说明机制怎样影响加入意愿，检查阶段限制。

S436.reference: I often laugh when a friend notices something ordinary that the rest of us have overlooked. For example, someone might point out that we have all ordered exactly the same meal after discussing the menu for ten minutes. I enjoy that kind of shared observation more than a prepared joke. Nobody has to be embarrassed, and the humor comes from an experience that we all recognize.
S436.explanation:
读懂：makes you laugh（令你发笑）是所问的反应；说与朋友相处时的一种情境。
解析：参考用大家点同一餐的细节说明共同观察，不要求讲完整笑话。
下次：听到幽默情境→选具体共同经历→说明好笑之处，检查不是只说朋友很有趣。

S437.reference: During a group presentation, our opening slide appeared upside down. We were nervous, but one teammate said that we were giving everyone a new perspective. People laughed, and we took a moment to correct the slide. The comment did not solve the technical problem, but it reduced the tension enough for us to continue calmly. It also focused on the situation rather than blaming a person.
S437.explanation:
读懂：讲幽默缓解尴尬的一次经历；awkward 指“尴尬的”。
解析：示例区分笑话减轻紧张与实际修复投影，作用没有被夸大成解决所有问题。
下次：听到缓解尴尬→讲原问题和幽默动作→说具体效果，检查因果不过度。

S438.reference: No. Humor often depends on shared knowledge, and new acquaintances may not understand what a speaker means. A comment intended to be playful can sound dismissive without that background. I would begin by listening and finding common interests. Humor may develop naturally after that. I do not think a person has to be funny to make a good first impression; clear interest in the other person can be enough.
S438.explanation:
读懂：评价初次见面时幽默是否总有用；always 限定“所有情况”。
解析：参考用共同背景不足说明误解风险，再给倾听方法；不等于所有幽默都不合适。
下次：听到绝对作用→找成立或不成立的条件→用交流后果支持，检查范围准确。

S439.reference: The speaker should clarify the meaning briefly and acknowledge that the comment did not come across as intended. Repeating that it was only a joke may make the other person feel that their reaction is the problem. A simple explanation or apology can help the group return to the topic. Later, the speaker can think about why the wording was unclear instead of demanding that everyone share the same sense of humor.
S439.explanation:
读懂：轻松玩笑被误解后，说话者如何处理；lighthearted 是“轻松的”。
解析：参考说明澄清、承认表达效果和回到话题，重点是修复沟通而非强迫对方发笑。
下次：听到表达误解→先澄清实际意思→回应影响并回到话题，检查行动可执行。

S440.reference: I try to use the person's name once in a natural part of the conversation and connect it with something we discussed. After a club meeting, I might remember that Maya is the person who asked about the photography trip. I avoid inventing a complicated memory system on the spot. Paying attention to one real detail about the conversation works better for me than repeating a name silently without listening.
S440.explanation:
读懂：just met（刚认识）限定人物；说明怎样记住他们的名字。
解析：示例把姓名与真实交谈细节相连，方法要同时说明怎样使用；名字只是虚构示例。
下次：听到记名方法→给一步实际动作→用情境展示，检查没有忽略倾听。

S441.reference: I ask the person to say it again and then try repeating it. I would rather make a small effort at the beginning than keep avoiding their name. If I still find a sound difficult, I explain that I am practicing instead of pretending that I have understood perfectly. Most importantly, I use the form the person prefers rather than choosing a shorter name for my own convenience.
S441.explanation:
读懂：不确定姓名读法时会怎样做；pronounce 指“发音”。
解析：参考包含询问、尝试和尊重本人称呼，普通沟通办法即可，不考语音学知识。
下次：听到发音不确定→描述求助与尝试→检查称呼由本人偏好决定。

S442.reference: Yes, because a large group can otherwise feel impersonal. When an organizer remembers my name at a second meeting, I feel that my earlier participation was noticed. That does not mean everyone must remember every name immediately. Name labels and brief introductions can help. The effort matters most when it supports real conversation, rather than becoming a test that makes people anxious about forgetting someone.
S442.explanation:
读懂：make a difference（产生影响）是评价重点；讨论在大群体中记名字的小努力。
解析：参考通过被记住的感受说明价值，同时区分自然交流与强求记忆；不同体验也可。
下次：听到小行为影响→给具体互动→连接它与群体感受，检查不是只有抽象赞同。

S443.reference: I would let students indicate how they prefer to be addressed. A single formal rule may seem simple, but it can produce names that people rarely use or do not feel comfortable hearing in conversation. The teacher could keep a clear class list connecting each preferred name with the official record. That preserves practical organization while allowing everyday interaction to reflect the student's own preference.
S443.explanation:
读懂：be addressed（被称呼）是这里的含义；比较学生自选称呼与统一正式规则。
解析：参考把偏好与名单对应兼顾，未要求改变正式记录；统一方案也可论证便利性。
下次：听到称呼规则→区分日常交流与记录需要→说明安排，检查回应两种功能。

S444.reference: I prepare my bag before going to bed. It only takes a few minutes, but it means that I do not have to look for chargers or notebooks when I am trying to leave in the morning. I usually check the next day's schedule first, so I bring what I actually need. The routine is useful because it removes several small decisions from a time when I am often rushed.
S444.explanation:
读懂：a small routine（一个小习惯）是范围；说明它怎样让日常生活更方便。
解析：示例把前晚整理包与早晨减少寻找联系起来；需要具体便利，不只说习惯很好。
下次：听到惯例作用→说固定动作和时点→连接避免的麻烦，检查因果明确。

S445.reference: I normally took the same route to class, but one day a path was closed and I walked past a different building. I noticed a small exhibition of student drawings in its entrance hall. After looking at it, I began checking that hall every few weeks. The route change was inconvenient at first, but it introduced me to a part of campus that I had been passing without seeing.
S445.explanation:
读懂：notice something new（注意到新事物）是结果；讲改变熟悉惯例后的经历。
解析：参考交代封路、换道、看到展览及后续，发现由变化引起；不需特殊旅行经历。
下次：听到惯例变化→对照原做法与新做法→指出具体发现，检查联系。

S446.reference: For me, a routine can make more room for creativity. If I have a regular time and place to draw, I spend less energy deciding whether to begin. Once I start, the work itself can be unpredictable. The problem is not repeating the starting habit but refusing to try a different idea during the activity. A stable beginning and an open approach to the work can fit together.
S446.explanation:
读懂：评价惯例与创造力的关系；creativity 是“创造力”。
解析：参考区分固定开始方式与作品内容变化，解释二者可以并存；限制创造的观点也可支持。
下次：听到两个概念冲突→拆清各自指什么→用实例说明关系，检查不是只下结论。

S447.reference: I would keep the basic format unless members identify a problem. People may return partly because they know what to expect and enjoy the current activities. Change is not automatically an improvement. The organizers could introduce one optional new activity at the end of a meeting and ask for reactions. That gives them information without replacing something successful simply because it has become familiar to the people organizing it.
S447.explanation:
读懂：popular（受欢迎的）是已知条件；评价持续一年同一形式的周会是否该改。
解析：参考保留成功形式并小范围试新，回应受欢迎这个已知条件；改变也需说明收益。
下次：听到是否改动现有做法→先利用题干效果信息→比较变化收益与代价，检查不为变化而变化。

S448.reference: I enjoy making simple cards for friends. I use paper, a pen, and sometimes a small drawing connected with the person receiving the card. I am not especially skilled at drawing, but I like deciding which detail will make the card feel personal. Because each card is small, I can usually finish it in one evening. Completing something tangible is part of the pleasure for me.
S448.explanation:
读懂：making or creating（制作或创作）是题目所问的活动；说明空闲时喜欢做什么。
解析：示例给出卡片、做法和乐趣，承认技能普通也能完整回答。
下次：听到创作偏好→说一种产物→给制作细节与喜欢的原因，检查具体。

S449.reference: I once wanted to wrap a friend's gift but had no wrapping paper. I used a plain paper bag and drew a simple map of places we had visited together. The package looked different from what I had planned, but my friend kept the drawing afterward. Working with what I had made me think about a personal detail that I might not have added to ordinary wrapping paper.
S449.explanation:
读懂：without having all the materials（没有全部所需材料）是限制；讲当时怎样完成制作。
解析：参考说明缺包装纸、替代材料与个人化地图，限制如何改变设计清楚可见。
下次：听到材料不足→明确缺什么与用什么→讲替代带来的结果，检查没有跳过过程。

S450.reference: They can help, but I would not say that more limits always produce better work. A small set of materials can give a beginner somewhere to start, while a strict deadline can make it difficult to develop a promising idea. I find one clear constraint useful, such as using only two colors. It gives the project a direction while leaving enough choices for me to explore.
S450.explanation:
读懂：limits on time or materials（时间或材料限制）是讨论条件；评价它们对创作的作用。
解析：参考区分限制类型和程度，用两种颜色说明适量约束；不把限制越多越好当结论。
下次：听到约束效果→明确哪种限制→用选择空间解释利弊，检查程度范围。

S451.reference: I would give everyone identical basic materials. That makes the results easier to compare and prevents the challenge from becoming a contest over who can obtain the most impressive supplies. The interest would come from seeing different uses of the same things. Students could explain their choices afterward, so an unusual but simple design could receive attention even if it did not look as polished as someone else's work.
S451.explanation:
读懂：identical materials（完全相同的材料）与自由选材形成选择；为学生设计挑战作决定。
解析：参考支持统一材料，连接比较公平与不同用法；其他选择可强调表达自由。
下次：听到竞赛资源安排→选材料规则→解释它怎样影响比较与创作，检查理由具体。

S452.reference: I prefer a demonstration first because I can see where each action happens. Written instructions sometimes use names for parts that I cannot yet identify. After watching once, I like having a short written guide so I can repeat the steps without asking again. For me, the two forms work well together, but seeing the whole process at the beginning makes it easier to understand the details.
S452.explanation:
读懂：a demonstration（一次演示）是文字说明之外的选择；解释学习陌生东西时的偏好。
解析：参考先选演示并解释识别部件的帮助，再说明文字后续用途；主偏好清楚。
下次：听到方式偏好→先选主要方式→把优点连到学习困难，检查不是只列两者。

S453.reference: An assignment once asked us to submit a brief response, but it did not say whether that meant a paragraph or several pages. I asked the teacher what a successful response needed to include. She explained that we should make one point and support it with an example. That answer helped more than a word limit would have, because it clarified the purpose of the task.
S453.explanation:
读懂：unclear（不清楚的）限定指令；讲遇到这种情况时怎样弄清要做什么。
解析：参考明确简短的歧义，询问后得到内容要求；回答要包含解决过程。
下次：听到不清楚的指令→指出具体缺口→讲求证与获得的信息，检查最终知道如何做。

S454.reference: I prefer a short explanation of why the important steps matter. If I understand the purpose, I can recognize whether I have completed the step correctly and adapt when something looks different. However, explaining every minor detail can hide the main sequence. A useful guide might show the essential actions clearly and put the reasons beside the steps where a mistake would change the result.
S454.explanation:
读懂：why each step matters（每步为什么重要）与只列操作形成比较；评价哪种说明更好。
解析：参考优先关键原因并保留顺序清晰，说明不是每个细节都需长解释。
下次：听到说明详略→确定用户需要判断的部分→说明原因如何帮助执行，检查长度取舍。

S455.reference: I would ask someone unfamiliar with the activity to try the instructions while I watched without immediately helping. I would note where they paused, guessed, or looked for information that was missing. Afterward, I would ask what they thought each difficult step meant. Their attempt would show problems that I might overlook because I already know the task. Then I would revise the confusing parts and try again.
S455.explanation:
读懂：a complete beginner（完全的新手）是目标读者；说明怎样检验自己写的步骤能否被执行。
解析：参考用实际尝试、观察卡点与回问验证，证据来自执行行为而非作者自认为清楚。
下次：听到验证可理解性→让目标用户尝试→观察并核对理解，检查方法能暴露具体问题。

S456.reference: I do not mind washing dishes after a shared meal. The task has a clear beginning and ending, and I can see the result immediately. I also like having a few quiet minutes while other people put food away. It is not something I would call a hobby, but it feels manageable. I find tasks with an obvious finish easier than organizing a room that can always be improved.
S456.explanation:
读懂：not mind（不介意）不等于必须最喜欢；选一项家务并解释。
解析：示例从清楚终点和即时结果解释洗碗偏好；无需把家务说成爱好。
下次：听到家务偏好→选具体任务→说其哪项特点适合你，检查理由与任务相连。

S457.reference: When I shared an apartment, each person chose one regular task, and we rotated the remaining small jobs each week. I usually took care of the kitchen floor because I was home early on Fridays. We changed the arrangement when someone's schedule became busy. The system worked better than expecting people to notice what needed doing, because everyone knew which tasks were theirs.
S457.explanation:
读懂：shared responsibilities（分担责任）是重点；讲与同住者的一种具体安排。
解析：参考说明固定任务、轮换和日程调整，交代为何有效；具体家庭结构不限。
下次：听到分工经历→讲谁负责什么及如何确定→补运行结果，检查分配机制明确。

S458.reference: I would consider time and effort. One task, such as planning meals and buying ingredients, may involve more work than several quick jobs combined. Counting only the number of tasks can hide that difference. People should also discuss which jobs they find difficult or easy. The goal is an arrangement that feels fair over time, rather than a list that has the same number of lines under every name.
S458.explanation:
读懂：equally by number（按数量平均）与按耗时精力形成比较；评价家务怎样分配。
解析：参考用采购计划的隐性工作解释只数件数的局限；另一种方法也可支持。
下次：听到公平分配→确定比较单位→用具体劳动说明标准，检查没有只喊平均。

S459.reference: The group could occasionally describe the work behind each regular task, including preparation and checking supplies. A short conversation may reveal effort that is easy to miss. They could then agree on broad responsibilities and ask whether anyone feels overloaded. I would avoid recording every minute, because that might turn ordinary cooperation into a competition. The aim is recognition and a workable arrangement, not proving who has contributed the most.
S459.explanation:
读懂：without keeping a strict score（不严格逐项计分）是限制；说明怎样让隐性劳动更清楚。
解析：参考通过简短交流呈现准备工作，再调整责任，回应可见性与不过度计较两项要求。
下次：听到透明但不计分→提出轻量沟通方式→解释怎样支持调整，检查未变成精细打分表。

S460.reference: I often photograph small details in places I walk through, such as an unusual doorway or a pattern of shadows. I rarely plan those pictures in advance. Taking them makes me stop and look at something I might otherwise pass. I usually keep them for myself rather than sharing every image. Later, they remind me of what caught my attention on an ordinary day.
S460.explanation:
读懂：most often（最常）限定频率；说明日常通常拍什么。
解析：示例给出门和影子的细节，再说明拍摄习惯与用途；不需专业摄影经验。
下次：听到常拍对象→说具体类型→加一个常见情境，检查不只谈器材。

S461.reference: I have a blurry photograph of my friends cooking in a very small kitchen. The lighting is poor, and several people are partly outside the frame. Still, it reminds me of an evening when we laughed at our unsuccessful attempt to make a complicated meal. A clearer photograph might show everyone's face better, but this one captures the movement and confusion that made the evening memorable.
S461.explanation:
读懂：visual quality（视觉质量）与个人意义形成对照；讲一张画质不突出但对你有意义的照片。
解析：参考对照模糊构图与共同做饭记忆，解释价值不只在技术效果。
下次：听到画质与意义对照→各给一项特征→说明个人联系，检查两面都回应。

S462.reference: For me, taking too many photographs becomes distracting. I start thinking about which angle to capture rather than noticing what is happening around me. At a performance, for example, trying to photograph every moment would change the way I watch and listen. I prefer taking one or two pictures near the beginning and then putting the phone away. Someone who enjoys photography as the main activity may have a different experience.
S462.explanation:
读懂：distract them（使人分心）是一种可能影响；评价大量拍照对体验注意力的作用。
解析：参考明确个人负面体验，用演出说明注意转移；承认以摄影为活动时可能不同。
下次：听到行为影响注意→说明注意从哪里转到哪里→给情境证据，检查主判断清楚。

S463.reference: The club should make it easy for members to state that preference before photographs are shared. It could use pictures of the activity or the materials when a group photo would include someone who prefers privacy. Members should still be able to participate fully in the event. I would also let people review a proposed public image, because agreeing to attend an activity is not the same as choosing to appear in its publicity.
S463.explanation:
读懂：not to appear publicly（不公开露面）是部分成员意愿；建议怎样与社团分享照片的目标协调。
解析：参考提供事前选择和其他画面，同时保持参与机会；重点是兼顾展示与个人选择。
下次：听到公开展示冲突→先确认偏好→给替代展示方法，检查不以退出活动换隐私。

S464.reference: I usually ask what they disliked about it. If we are talking about a film or a song, their answer may point to something I did not notice. I do not feel that I have to persuade them to enjoy it too. Sometimes I explain what mattered to me, and we discover that we were looking for different things. That can make the conversation more interesting than simple agreement.
S464.explanation:
读懂：dislikes something you enjoy（不喜欢你喜欢的东西）是分歧；说明你通常怎样回应朋友。
解析：示例先询问依据，再比较关注点，回答的是实际互动而非强求一致。
下次：听到偏好分歧→讲你的第一步→用交流结果解释，检查行动明确。

S465.reference: I once thought our club should hold every meeting in the evening because more rooms were available. Another member explained that some students had long journeys home and would leave before the activity ended. I had not considered that difficulty. We tried an afternoon meeting, and several new people attended. Their experience changed my view of what a convenient time meant for the group.
S465.explanation:
读懂：changed your mind（改变了你的想法）是结果；讲另一个人的观点怎样产生影响。
解析：参考列原方案、未考虑的通勤问题与新安排结果，转变依据具体。
下次：听到改变观点→先说原判断→给触发信息与新判断，检查不是无理由改口。

S466.reference: No. A discussion can be useful when people understand the reasons behind a disagreement more clearly. If two members prefer different event plans, learning what each one values may help them cooperate later even if they still vote differently. Agreement is useful when a decision is needed, but it is not the only possible result. Identifying the real question can be progress too.
S466.explanation:
读懂：评价讨论是否只有一致结论才算成功；only 限定唯一标准。
解析：参考提出理解分歧的价值，同时保留决策时需要结论的情境。
下次：听到唯一成功标准→检验其他有价值结果→举例说明，检查回应 only。

S467.reference: The leader could give the person a clear opportunity to explain the view, then invite others to respond to its main point. A brief speaking limit should apply to everyone, including people who agree with the majority. The leader can also summarize the concern before moving on, so it is not simply lost. Being heard does not require unlimited time, but it does require an accurate response to the idea.
S467.explanation:
读懂：a minority view（少数人的观点）需要被听见；说明怎样同时避免一人主导整场会议。
解析：参考把平等发言时间与准确回应结合，两项目标均有具体措施。
下次：听到表达权与时间冲突→给同一流程与时间边界→检查观点得到回应而非仅被打断。

S468.reference: I would like to become comfortable cooking a few meals without following every line of a recipe. I enjoy inviting friends over, but I currently spend too much time checking instructions. Knowing a small set of dishes well would make those evenings more relaxed. I am not trying to become an expert cook. I want enough confidence to focus on the people at the table as well as the food.
S468.explanation:
读懂：matter to you（对你重要）要求解释意义；提出一个个人目标并说明原因。
解析：参考用独立做几道菜连接招待朋友的愿望，目标具体且范围合理。
下次：听到目标及意义→给可观察的目标→解释个人用途，检查不是只说提升自己。

S469.reference: I identify a small result that I could achieve within a week. When I wanted to read more in English, I began with a short article each morning rather than choosing a difficult novel. Finishing those articles gave me a routine and showed me which topics held my interest. The larger goal remained, but I had something clear to do today instead of only imagining a distant result.
S469.explanation:
读懂：说明怎样让大目标更易着手；manageable 指“能应付的”。
解析：参考通过一周内可完成的小结果和每日短文说明拆解方法。
下次：听到大目标→提出近期可完成单位→用例子检查是否能立即行动。

S470.reference: I would share it with one person who can offer useful support, rather than announce it widely. Talking can help me turn a vague wish into a specific plan, and a friend may notice obstacles I have missed. A public announcement could create pressure to continue even if the goal needs changing. The value of sharing depends more on the listener than on how many people hear about it.
S470.explanation:
读懂：keep it private（暂不公开）与先分享形成比较；评价新目标应何时告诉别人。
解析：参考提出有限分享，解释支持与压力之间取舍；不是必须完全公开或完全保密。
下次：听到分享时机选择→明确对象与范围→解释它如何影响行动，检查主方案清楚。

S471.reference: Changing a goal is sensible when new experience shows that it no longer serves the reason I chose it. For example, someone aiming to perform alone might discover that they enjoy arranging music for a group much more. I would first ask whether the problem is a temporary difficulty or a change in what matters. The effort already spent can still be useful even when the final direction changes.
S471.explanation:
读懂：giving up too easily（过于轻易放弃）是要区分的情况；说明何时改目标属于合理决定。
解析：参考用最初目的、新经验和暂时困难区分判断；已付出努力不是必须坚持原目标的唯一理由。
下次：听到是否该改目标→回看最初目的→区分暂时障碍与方向变化，检查判断有依据。

S472.reference: I usually ask someone who has recently done a similar task, rather than automatically asking my closest friend. If I need help finding a room on campus, a person who studies in that building may give the clearest answer. I try to explain exactly what I have already tried. That makes the request easier to respond to and shows that I value the other person's time.
S472.explanation:
读懂：whom（谁）问求助对象；说明遇到小任务通常找谁帮助。
解析：参考按相关经验选人并解释理由，问题无需列真实姓名。
下次：听到求助对象→给选择标准→用小任务说明，检查标准与帮助内容有关。

S473.reference: I was editing a short report and had read it so many times that I no longer noticed missing steps. A classmate offered to read the introduction. She asked one question that showed I had not explained why the topic mattered. I added a few sentences, and the report became easier to follow. Accepting help did not mean handing over the work; it gave me a reader's perspective.
S473.explanation:
读懂：accepting help（接受帮助）是起因；讲它怎样改善一次任务。
解析：参考说明自身盲点、同学的问题与实际修改，保留作者自己完成的过程。
下次：听到帮助带来改善→指出原困难→连接外部帮助与新结果，检查帮助作用具体。

S474.reference: Not necessarily. Independence includes knowing when another person's knowledge can help me make a better decision. If I ask someone to show me a method and then practice it myself, I may need less help next time. The important difference is whether I am learning or simply passing every difficult task to someone else. A focused question can be part of taking responsibility for the work.
S474.explanation:
读懂：less independent（较不独立）是待评价的判断；讨论求助是否会产生这种结果。
解析：参考区分学习方法与长期转交任务，解释求助如何支持以后独立；可有不同观点。
下次：听到能力判断→明确能力含义→用求助后行动说明，检查不是仅凭是否求助下结论。

S475.reference: I would thank the friend and explain which part of the help would be most useful. For example, I might say that I want to try the main task myself but would appreciate someone checking the result. That gives the offer a clear place instead of simply saying no. I would also explain that practicing independently matters to me, so the limit is about my learning rather than a lack of trust.
S475.explanation:
读懂：more help than you need（超过需要的帮助）是问题；说明怎样保留自主空间又照顾朋友感受。
解析：参考感谢、明确所需部分并解释练习目的，限制帮助不等于否定朋友。
下次：听到帮助与自主冲突→给具体可接受范围→说明原因，检查回应既明确又有礼貌。

S476.reference: I would try a beginner pottery class. I like making things with my hands, and the material seems different from the paper and pencils I usually use. I would expect my first object to look uneven, but I would still enjoy seeing how its shape changes while I work. My goal for the first lesson would be understanding a few basic movements rather than producing something impressive.
S476.explanation:
读懂：a complete beginner（完全的新手）是设定；说即使零基础也愿尝试的活动。
解析：参考明确陶艺、兴趣和首课目标，允许初次结果不完美。
下次：听到新活动意愿→选活动→连接已有兴趣和初步期待，检查不靠声称天赋。

S477.reference: At my first chess club meeting, I worried that I would slow everyone down. One member offered a short practice game and explained her thinking between moves. That helped me see the meeting as a place to learn rather than a test of whether I belonged. I still lost the game, but I left wanting to return because I understood a little more than when I arrived.
S477.explanation:
读懂：already had experience（已经有经验）描述其他人；讲加入这种活动时自己的感受。
解析：参考交代紧张、练习中的支持及离开时的变化，输赢不是唯一结果。
下次：听到新手感受→说起初情绪→给改变或维持情绪的具体经历，检查个人体验清楚。

S478.reference: No. I can enjoy an activity because of the process, the people, or the small improvements I notice. When I draw with friends, I like comparing what each of us noticed, even though our technical skills differ. Being more skilled may open new possibilities, but waiting until I am good enough would remove the chance to discover whether I enjoy the activity in the first place.
S478.explanation:
读懂：necessary（必要的）问的是必需条件；评价是否必须擅长才能享受活动。
解析：参考提出过程、同伴与小进步等其他快乐来源，同时承认熟练有作用。
下次：听到必要条件→找不依赖该条件的情境→用体验说明，检查没有否定技能全部价值。

S479.reference: The club could separate open practice sessions from the selection for a public event. Beginners would have a genuine place to learn, while performance requirements could remain clear. It could also offer several forms of contribution, such as assisting with presentation or showing work in a smaller informal display. The key is to explain the standards early and provide a path toward them, rather than welcoming people in name but excluding them from every meaningful activity.
S479.explanation:
读懂：maintaining standards（维持标准）是另一目标；说明社团怎样兼顾新手参与与公开成果质量。
解析：参考给开放练习、明确标准及不同参与方式，两个目标都有路径；不要求降低所有标准。
下次：听到开放与质量双要求→区分活动阶段→给成长和参与途径，检查不是空喊欢迎。
